subject: Introduction to the simmering tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the looming threat of war
place: Strait of Hormuz, Bandar Abbas, USS Truxtun
grounding_notes: Establish the geopolitical chokepoint and introduce the two military POVs who will anchor the naval conflict.

included_characters.role_in_chapter: Executive Officer of the USS Truxtun

quality_parameters.philosophical_depth: explore the illusion of control and the distance between decision-makers and sufferers
quality_parameters.metaphorical_richness: use sea, gate, fire, and machine imagery consistently
quality_parameters.accessibility: clear to adult thriller readers without military background
quality_parameters.timelessness: echo classical questions of responsibility and mercy

chapter_summary: The world wakes to news that the Panama-flagged tanker has exploded across the strait; Sarah Lin watches the CIC fill with real-time catastrophe while Reza Sharifi stands on Qeshm Island and sees the same smoke from the other shore, and in Washington and London the first cost is measured in futures rather than blood. The seed scene must open on the fragile morning calm, introduce the two commanders as professionals trained to hesitate, then break that calm with the blast and the first warning shots, ending with the understanding that no single decision started the fire but every next one may spread it.
theme: the illusion of control in complex geopolitical systems
